messages:
alex: FYI I have a small reproducer that shows pagetable shadowwalks + KV cache growth on a mixed NVLink/PCIe cluster (H100 + MI250x in the same job).

alex: Symptoms: after ~30k tokens user sessions start seeing token emission stalls, GPU memory grows on the H100 worker, and eviction churn skyrockets. longctx usage + fragmentation rises steadily.

alex: Repro steps in brief:
```
# start model on h100 (nvlink mesh)
./run_infer --model redwood/7b --device h100 --kv-page-size 1MB --batch-scheduler round_robin
# spawn tail worker on mi250x via pcie slot
./worker --device mi250x --role spill
# run chat workload with repeated long-contexts (~64k tokens)
python stress_longctx.py --sessions 200 --seq 64000
```

devon: can you drop the perf traces? which kernel path used when it blows up?

maria: attaching snippets from perf and trace logs (summary):
```
- kv_cache: evict_rate x10 after 28k tokens
- page_table: shadow_walk latency spike at 2024-11-03T14:23
- kernel_select: switched to tiled-kv kernel for seq>8192
- owner_swap: seen mixed OWNER_IDs in PT entries when walking cross-gpu
```

maria: also saw repeated `PAGE_LOCK_RETRY` events in the h100 driver logs, stacked with NVLink link resets (low-level). stack traces point to the pagetable walk code path.

jn: interesting — I ran a bisect on the runtime changes and the regression correlates with the kernel-selection heuristic that started preferring tiled kernels for large seqs (PR: runtime#4281). The tiled kernel leaks a little metadata on fallback in our testing env.

samira: hypothesis: when kernel selector switches mid-session, we emit a different layout for the KV pages and the pager's shadow metadata isn't atomically updated across GPUs. Cross-GPU walkers can end up reading stale owner pointers and repinning old page ranges -> leakage and eviction thrash.

alex: that matches what I saw: H100 holds onto pages even though MI250x initiated the eviction; NVLink commands complete but the PT entries still show the old owner. Looks like a memory ordering or write-combine issue across the different vendor drivers.

devon: can you attach the minimal repro please? I'll try with `KV_DEBUG=1` and capture `kvcache_dump` + `pt_walk` traces.

alex: uploaded repro gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/repro-6633331111

runtime-bot: deploy-check: reproducible job created (id: job-6633331111-repro). Logs available: https://ci.internal/jobs/job-6633331111

maria: I ran the repro with extra instrumentation. Notable trace snippet:
```
[PT_WALK] walker=mi250x id=0x7f3a owner=0x42 -> read pt entry (owner=0x42)
[NVLINK_SYNC] h100 ack
[PT_UPDATE] walker=h100 id=0x9f1 owner=0x9f1 -> wrote tombstone
[PT_WALK] walker=mi250x id=0x7f3a -> read pt entry (owner=0x42)  # stale
```

maria: also saw sequence numbers not monotonically increasing for the same page when read by a different GPU.

jn: two-pronged mitigation options:
- short-term: increase serialization around PT updates when crossing vendor boundaries (costly but quick)
- medium-term: canonicalize kernel page layouts so selector switches do a transactional swap (update meta then flip pointer)

samira: +1 for transactional swap; might be a bit invasive.

devon: for triage we should: 1) add PT write fences when evicting across GPUs, 2) add a debug check to detect owner mismatch on walk and trigger a recovery path instead of leaking page.

alex: agreed. I can prototype a fenced PT update and push a test. If tests pass, we can roll as a hotfix for Dedicated clusters with mixed GPUs.

maria: perf note — fenced PT update will add ~1.2% latency in our microbench batch but reduces eviction churn massively in repro. Worth it for now.

samira: I'll open an RFC doc outlining transactional layout swap design, include kernel selector invariants we need.

jn: owners:
- alex: repro + fenced-pt patch
- devon: add debug owner-mismatch detector + tests
- samira: RFC + long-term design
- maria: perf validation on H100/MI250x matrix

alex: created PR draft: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/5120

devon: I'll run the detector with CI matrix (h100/mi250x/rtx) and post results.

maria: one more ask — please capture `nvidia-smi topo -m` and relevant ROCm topology so infra can reproduce exact bus layout.

alex: added topology capture to repro.

runtime-bot: scheduled a follow-up sync on #eng-runtime for 2024-11-07 16:00 UTC

alex: thanks all, will update PR and ping next steps. :thumbsup:
